decision: runner/decomposed_drafting.py::_default_claude_drafter resolves its provider through runner.transport.config.resolve_provider_config(): claude_cli keeps the Claude CLI transport with _DRAFTER_MODEL; bedrock_converse and the other tool-calling backends draft through run_tool_loop with the resolved model, Read/Glob confined to _GROUNDING_INPUTS; under ORCHESTRATOR_PRODUCTION_MODE=true a non-production backend is refused at resolution, so the drafter never reaches the CLI. _DRAFTER_MAX_TOKENS becomes 32000. decisions.question: Where the routing lives (point 1)
decisions.answer: (a) In runner/decomposed_drafting.py only. _default_claude_drafter resolves resolve_provider_config(); claude_cli keeps runner.claude_transport.invoke_claude_text; bedrock_converse builds build_converse_backend(config, tools=[READ_TOOL_SCHEMA, GLOB_TOOL_SCHEMA], temperature=0.0, max_tokens=_DRAFTER_MAX_TOKENS); other backends build_openai_backend with the same tools; both drive run_tool_loop. runner/skill_runtime.py (run_skill) is not touched.
decisions.reason: Operator's '1a'. The ticket's 'as the skill runtime does', with run_skill untouched so criterion 3 holds by construction.
decisions.consequence: runner/decomposed_drafting.py; the diff names no other runner/ module except runner/claude_transport.py (R10-D6).

decisions.question: Which backends (point 2)
decisions.answer: (a) The skill runtime's set: claude_cli, bedrock_converse, and the OpenAI-compatible tool-calling backends. A backend whose capabilities have tool_calling False is refused with DecomposedDraftingError ('does not support tool calling'), because TAPM needs tools.
decisions.reason: Operator's '2a'. Parity with the skill runtime; production mode narrows the set to bedrock_converse anyway (PRODUCTION_BACKENDS).

decisions.question: Model, limits, timeout (point 3)
decisions.answer: (a) Non-CLI backends draft with ProviderConfig.model (build_converse_backend / build_openai_backend refuse a missing one with ValueError 'model is required'); the CLI path keeps _DRAFTER_MODEL (claude-opus-4-8). Timeout _DRAFTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (1800 s) is the tool loop's wall-clock budget; max_rounds stays the loop default (25). max_tokens: R10-D15.
decisions.reason: Operator's '3a'. On the host the model is the runtime secret's ORCHESTRATOR_TRANSPORT_MODEL (OD7-orchestrator), which AN1c already counts under production mode (R9e-D8).

decisions.question: TAPM boundary (point 4)
decisions.answer: (a) run_tool_loop(allowed_prefixes=list(_GROUNDING_INPUTS)): the Python tool executor refuses a Read or Glob outside the declared grounding inputs. The CLI path keeps its existing behaviour (the CLI has no such sandbox).
decisions.reason: Operator's '4a'. The executor's declared-input boundary is the same one the skill runtime uses for reads_from.

decisions.question: Resolution caching (point 5)
decisions.answer: (a) Resolved once per _default_claude_drafter(...) call (one per section), no process cache. The backend is built in the same place, so a resolution or configuration error (production-mode refusal, missing model, no tool calling) raises before draft_section_decomposed removes prior drafts.
decisions.reason: Operator's '5a'. A process cache would carry a configuration across tests (the F-R9-1 trap) and across runs in one process.

decisions.question: Defence in depth in the CLI transport (point 6)
decisions.answer: (a) runner.claude_transport.invoke_claude_text calls _refuse_under_production_mode() first: under ORCHESTRATOR_PRODUCTION_MODE=true it raises ClaudeCLIProductionModeError (R10-D21) before resolve_claude_cli or any subprocess. The variable is read with is_production_mode's rule inside the transport, not by importing runner.transport.config, so the check never triggers that module's .env load (F-R9-4).
decisions.reason: Operator's '6a'. A future caller that bypasses provider resolution still fails closed. Checked before the change: every production-mode test that reaches the CLI transport mocks it (tests/test_persistence_policy.py patches runner.skill_runtime.invoke_claude_text); the only real CLI caller under production mode would be harness/commands/_subscription_judge.py, which must fail closed on the host (no CLI there).

decisions.question: The DC-35 gap in the drafter's capture (point 7)
decisions.answer: (a) Content capture honours runner.persistence_policy: at level full the drafter writes <sub>.response.txt and, on a transport failure, <sub>.transport_failure.txt (stdout/stderr) as before; at level metadata (always under production mode) it writes only <sub>.response_meta.json: sub_section_id, backend, model, diagnostic_level, response_chars, tool-loop rounds, files_read count, exhausted_rounds, and on failure exception_class and sanitize_error_message(str(exc)).
decisions.reason: Operator's '7a'. Same function, same production path; DC-35 says metadata level writes no prompt or response content.
decisions.consequence: tests/runner/test_decomposed_drafting_transport.py::TestDiagnosticLevel (four tests: metadata success, metadata parse failure, metadata transport failure, full).

decisions.question: The criterion-1 test (point 8)
decisions.answer: (a) New tests/runner/test_decomposed_drafting_transport.py: production mode with BEDROCK_CONVERSE_EU, a sentinel Region and model, boto3.client replaced by a scripted fake Converse client (tests/harness/test_converse_judge.py pattern), and invoke_claude_text and resolve_claude_cli replaced by tripwires; production mode with a claude_cli configuration (backend, preset CLAUDE_REFERENCE, backend unset) refused with a production-mode ValueError before any CLI call; the same through draft_section_decomposed; a direct invoke_claude_text call refused. Every test pins os.environ with clear=True and resets the diagnostic-level cache.
decisions.reason: Operator's '8a'. Shown failing on the start commit before the change: evidence_v2/R10/R10_02_head-criterion1.txt (7 failed: six 'the Claude CLI transport was called', one 'the claude executable was resolved').

decisions.question: Existing tests amended on purpose (point 9)
decisions.answer: (a) TestProductionDrafterPromptHardening in tests/runner/test_excellence_decomposed_drafting.py gains an autouse fixture pinning a non-production claude_cli environment (ORCHESTRATOR_TRANSPORT_PRESET=CLAUDE_REFERENCE, clear=True) and resetting the diagnostic-level cache; the test bodies are unchanged. See amended_test_ids.
decisions.reason: Operator's '9a'. The two tests patch invoke_claude_text and rely on the drafter reaching it; the drafter now resolves first, so an unpinned environment (a leaked .env.harness, F-R9-1) could route them elsewhere.

Step 03 records the diff stat.
decisions.reason: Operator's '10a'. CLAUDE.md section 17: R10 changes which configured runtime transport a node body's Claude call goes through (17.5.2), not the call graph (17.1), the contracts (17.4) or the failure semantics (17.3): a resolution or transport failure still raises out of draft_section_decomposed and becomes an agent-body failure in run_agent (~1298).

decisions.question: Baseline commit (point 13)
decisions.answer: (a) There is no 'starting R10' commit: the R10 handoff went into 265f88d 'tick R9e'. The baseline ran on 265f88d; recorded as a deviation from handoff section 5 step 1. No commit in round 1.

decisions.question: Line endings (point 14)
decisions.answer: (a) runner/decomposed_drafting.py, runner/claude_transport.py and tests/runner/test_excellence_decomposed_drafting.py are CRLF in the working copy (git ls-files --eol: i/lf w/crlf; the handoff said LF). Each edited file kept its endings (exact-match, all-or-nothing read-modify-write, R9e-D18); the new test file is written CRLF like its neighbours; this record is LF like the other records.
decisions.reason: Operator's '14a'.
decisions.consequence: No line-ending churn in the diff under the workstation's core.autocrlf.

decisions.question: max_tokens (point 15)
decisions.answer: (a) _DRAFTER_MAX_TOKENS becomes 32000 (was 8000). The claude -p transport ignores max_tokens (its ceiling is _MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_DEFAULT, 32000, via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS), so the CLI path is unchanged in effect; Converse and the OpenAI-compatible backends enforce it.
decisions.reason: Operator's '15a'. 8000 on Converse would cut a long sub-section reply mid-object (the run 0395b136 class: ~30.7k chars, ~8k tokens) and fail the node closed for a reason the CLI never had.
decisions.consequence: tests/runner/test_decomposed_drafting_transport.py::...::test_production_converse_drafts_without_the_cli asserts maxTokens 32000. Risk kept, not changed: BedrockConverseBackend's read_timeout is 600 s per request.

decisions.question: Empty or exhausted tool loop (point 16)
decisions.answer: (a) run_tool_loop signals its round limit or wall-clock deadline with exhausted_rounds=True and possibly empty text, not an exception. The drafter raises DecomposedDraftingError when exhausted_rounds is True or the text is empty, after writing the metadata record.
decisions.reason: Operator's '16a'. Text from a loop that did not finish is not a final reply; fail closed (17.5.4).

decisions.question: Response excerpt in the error message (point 17)
decisions.answer: (a) _parse_drafter_response gains include_excerpt (default True); the drafter passes False at level metadata, so the parse-failure message carries the response length but no excerpt. The message reaches AgentResult.failure_reason and run_summary.json, which are written at every level.
decisions.reason: Operator's '17a'.

decisions.question: Throttling (point 20)

decisions.reason: Operator's '20a'; 17.5.4 forbids a retry in the runtime.

decisions.question: Error type of the CLI refusal (point 21)
decisions.answer: (a) ClaudeCLIProductionModeError(ClaudeCLIUnavailableError) in runner/claude_transport.py; its message names ORCHESTRATOR_PRODUCTION_MODE=true. harness/commands/_subscription_judge.py does not retry ClaudeCLIUnavailableError; runner/skill_runtime.py classifies it CLI_UNAVAILABLE.
decisions.reason: Operator's '21a'. A plain ClaudeTransportError would be retried twice by the subscription judge.
decisions.consequence: tests/runner/test_decomposed_drafting_transport.py::TestCliTransportRefusesUnderProductionMode (asserts the type and the base class).
